module_title: Towards Independence (1939-1947) - Mutinies, Interim Government, and the Independence Act
introduction: This advanced level provides a critical analysis of the final blows to the British Empire (INA Trials, RIN Mutiny), the friction in forming the Interim Government, Attlee's Declaration, and the complex legal provisions of the Indian Independence Act of 1947.

core_concepts.title: INA Trials (Red Fort Trials - 1945)
core_concepts.description: The British tried three INA officers (Prem Sahgal, Shah Nawaz Khan, Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon) for treason. The nation united in their defense. Congress formed the 'INA Defence Committee' led by Bhulabhai Desai, Tej Bahadur Sapru, and Nehru.

core_concepts.title: Royal Indian Navy (RIN) Mutiny (1946)
core_concepts.description: In February 1946, Indian ratings (sailors) on the 'HMIS Talwar' mutinied against poor food and racial discrimination. They surrendered only after intervention by Sardar Patel and Jinnah.

core_concepts.title: Cabinet Mission and the 'Grouping' Controversy
core_concepts.description: The Mission proposed dividing provinces into three groups (A, B, C) and explicitly rejected the demand for Pakistan. However, the League saw 'Grouping' as a stepping stone to Pakistan, leading to a major constitutional clash with Congress.

core_concepts.title: Formation of the Interim Government (1946)
core_concepts.description: An Interim Government was formed in September 1946 under Jawaharlal Nehru. The Muslim League initially boycotted it but joined in October specifically to obstruct its functioning (Liaquat Ali Khan became the Finance Minister).

core_concepts.title: Attlee's Declaration & Indian Independence Act 1947
core_concepts.description: British PM Clement Attlee declared that the British would leave India by June 30, 1948. Based on Mountbatten's plan, the UK Parliament passed the Independence Act, creating two dominions and allowing princely states to join either or remain independent.

important_entities.name: Bhulabhai Desai
important_entities.significance: Successfully led the formidable team of lawyers defending the INA officers at the historic Red Fort trials.

important_entities.name: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
important_entities.significance: Foreseeing the danger of the 562 princely states remaining independent, he executed the monumental task of political integration of India.

important_entities.name: Clement Attlee
important_entities.significance: His Labour government came to power after WWII and adopted a more sympathetic and urgent approach toward Indian independence.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: The Interim Government was technically the Viceroy's Executive Council. The 'Viceroy' was its President, and 'Jawaharlal Nehru' was its 'Vice-President', not the Prime Minister.
Pay close attention: The Cabinet Mission report logically and explicitly 'REJECTED' the creation of a separate sovereign state of Pakistan.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: By putting officers of three major religions on trial together, the British unintentionally sparked unprecedented communal unity across India.

exam_strategy_tips: For Assertion-Reasoning questions, deeply understand how the 'Grouping of Provinces' clause in the Cabinet Mission Plan became the breaking point between Congress and the League.
A common direct question: Who was the Prime Minister of Britain when India got independence? Answer: Clement Attlee (Labour Party).
